originalText: In 2024, the Northstar team focused on encouraging more free users to move to paid plans. Unlike marketing campaigns viewed in isolation, upgrade prompts met people while they were already working on documents. The prompt catalog had not been reviewed recently. Working with a product manager and a product designer, my role as content designer was to rewrite these prompts so they communicated value clearly and helped people decide how to proceed.
rewrittenText:
In 2024, Northstar set out to increase free-to-paid conversion through its self-serve document-editing funnel. As content designer, I partnered with a product manager and a product designer to overhaul the application’s neglected catalog of in-product upgrade prompts.

Rather than relying on generic prompts, we mapped the copy directly to user context. We drew clear boundaries between three distinct situations: an active free allowance, an exhausted limit, and the intentional selection of a paid feature. The design rationale was deliberate: eliminate ambiguity by showing users exactly where they stood in their workflow and what the paid tier offered them at that moment.

Across the complete rollout, the upgrade-prompt program lifted paid conversion by 9% and added €200,000 in ARR. While these whole-program results belong to the combined efforts of product, design, and engineering rather than an isolated test of copy alone, they demonstrate how direct, state-aware language drives commercial momentum.

Maintains a confident cadence, pairing longer explanatory clauses with sharp, structured lists and direct takeaways to keep the reader engaged without relying on hollow buzzwords.

customInstructions: Write for product and content-design hiring readers. Remove the unnecessary marketing comparison and other familiar exposition. State the commercial objective directly. Use relevant context and the whole-program result from the project brief to explain my contribution clearly. Preserve attribution and distinguish the rationale from demonstrated outcomes. Return only the rewritten passage.
projectBrief: Fictional QA project. Northstar is a document-editing application. The team's objective was to increase free-to-paid conversion through its self-serve funnel. I was its content designer and wrote the prompt copy with a product manager and designer. We distinguished a remaining free allowance from an exhausted allowance and from a paid feature someone had selected. The content decisions made the current state and relevant paid value understandable. The upgrade-prompt program increased paid conversion by 9% and added €200,000 ARR; these are whole-program team results, not an isolated effect of a single prompt or solely my copy. No usability research or individual-copy causal test is established. Do not claim any. These are fictional test facts, not a real company's results.
